zh: 各位置的字符组彼此独立：第 i 组必须同时包含 x[i] 和 y[i]；要让整条正则不匹配 z，至少要有一个位置的组不包含 z[i]，而这只在 z[i] 与 x[i]、y[i] 都不同的位置才做得到。
要最长，就让每个位置都用 A..Z 全集 [ABC…Z]，只在一个可行位置删掉 z[i]，长度为 28n−1；删更多字符只会更短。所有候选只差在“哪个位置缩短”。
比较两个候选：在缩短的组里，被删字母的位置会出现更大的下一个字符（删 Z 时是 ]，而 Z 小于 ]），所以缩短组出现得越早字典序越大。从右往左找第一个满足 z[i]≠x[i] 且 z[i]≠y[i] 的位置，把它作为唯一缩短组，其余都是全集；找不到就输出 -1。输出可达约 2.8×10^7 个字符，要整体缓冲后一次输出。
en: Positions are independent: the i-th class must contain both x[i] and y[i]; for the whole regex to reject z, at least one class must omit z[i], which is possible only where z[i] differs from both x[i] and y[i].

For maximum length, use the full class [ABC...Z] at every position and remove z[i] at exactly one feasible position, giving length 28n - 1; removing more letters only makes it shorter. All candidates differ only in which position is shortened.

Comparing two candidates: inside the shortened class, the spot of the removed letter shows the next, larger character (when Z is removed it is ], and Z is smaller than ]), so the earlier the shortened class appears, the larger the string. Scan from right to left for the first i with z[i] != x[i] and z[i] != y[i], make it the only shortened class and use the full class everywhere else; if none exists, print -1. The output can be about 2.8 * 10^7 characters, so build it in a buffer and write it at once.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Each position is an independent character class. To match both x[i] and y[i], the class must contain both characters; for the whole string not to match z, at least one position must not contain z[i]. Hence a feasible position must have z[i] different from both x[i] and y[i].

The longest answer uses the full set A-Z at every position and removes z[i] at only one feasible position, giving length 28n-1. Removing more characters makes it shorter; removing at a position that does not satisfy the condition makes it fail to match x/y.

When one letter is removed at any feasible position, all other positions stay the same. After the removed character, the shortened class meets the larger next character (if Z is removed, it meets `]`; `Z` is still smaller than `]`), so a string whose shortened class appears earlier is lexicographically larger. Therefore choose the rightmost feasible position. If there is no feasible position, output `-1`.

## Proof of correctness

The i-th character class of any valid regex must contain x[i] and y[i]. To reject z, at least one class must not contain z[i]; that position must satisfy z[i] != x[i] and z[i] != y[i]. A full class has length 28 and a class shortened by one character has length 27, so any feasible answer has length at most 28n-1; removing z[i] at a single feasible position and using full classes everywhere else reaches the bound. When comparing candidates, everything before the first differing class is identical, and at the removed character the full class is smaller than the shortened class's next character (including the right bracket when Z is removed), so moving the single shortened class as far right as possible gives the lexicographic minimum. The algorithm scans from right to left to find the first feasible position and builds the answer that attains the bound, as required. If no such position exists, every class must contain the corresponding z[i], so any regex matching both x and y also matches z, and there is no solution.

## Complexity

Scanning the input is O(n) and building the output is O(n); extra working space O(1), output space O(n).

## Verification

The 163 inputs were checked by an independent oracle that enumerates every feasible exclusion position, builds the full candidates and compares the strings directly; in addition, all 3^6 = 729 combinations of x/y/z over A/B/C with length 2 were exhausted, enumerating every possible subset class at each position. The formal tests cover no solution, one or several feasible positions, excluding A/Z, and n=1000. Separately, an n=10^6 output was built locally to check its length and its match/mismatch properties. Two normally-returning wrong programs are each killed by formal cases.

## Source and this site's protocol

The pinned upstream OAMaster Pure Storage page/catalog labels #2 as Amazon Regex Generator, explicitly specifying uppercase letters/bracket classes, matching both x and y, rejecting z, longest with the lexicographically smallest among equal lengths, and gives n <= 10^6. The accompanying Python/Java/C++ reference code in the pinned commit all pick the earliest feasible position; this candidate is rewritten from the rules in the statement and corrected to the rightmost feasible position. Upstream has no stdin/stdout examples; this site adds the protocol of n on the first line followed by three lines x/y/z, plus validation of the A-Z character set.

A separate local file `OA LIST/Pure_Storage_OA/002_image.txt` labels its own #2 as Find Repetitions, which differs from the numbering of the pinned site/catalog. This candidate corresponds only to #2 of the pinned OAMaster Pure Storage page/catalog and does not mix in that local list.
